strings.title: The Crime Algorithm
strings.hint: The delivery app's programmer knew everyone's location in real time… who deleted a single line from the server log after the crime?
strings.solvedText:
The culprit: technical co-founder Karim Dawoud.

The victim, the founder and director, had discovered that Karim was secretly selling users' location data to a third party for millions. She planned to fire him and inform the authorities the next morning. Karim exploited the app's real-time knowledge of every driver and user's location. He lured her to an empty parking garage with a fake delivery request, killed her there, then deleted the only server log entry linking his phone to the crime scene. But he forgot the automatic backup.

The backup log placing his phone at the scene, the fake request issued from his administrator account, and the data-sale deal in his encrypted email proved his guilt.
strings.summary.text: Layan Murad, founder of a popular delivery app, was found murdered in an empty parking garage after being summoned by a delivery request she had never made. The app she built knew the real-time location of every user and driver in the city, a double-edged weapon that led her into a trap. After the crime, exactly one line was deleted from the server log… but the backup never forgets.

strings.summary.victim.name: Layan Murad
strings.summary.victim.job: Founder and director of a delivery app

strings.scene.address: Multistory parking garage — empty ground floor
strings.scene.intro: A garage almost deserted at night, with no functioning cameras. The request that drew the victim there originated inside the system, not from a real user. There was no theft: her phone and wallet remained. The crime was planned digitally and carried out physically.
strings.scene.photos[0].cap: The fake request notification on her phone
strings.scene.notes[0]: A delivery request from an administrator account, not a user
strings.scene.notes[1]: No theft — no immediate financial motive
strings.scene.notes[2]: One line was deleted from the server log after the crime
strings.scene.notes[3]: An automatic backup of the log remained untouched
strings.evidence[0].title: The Fake Request
strings.evidence[0].desc: A delivery request manually created through an administrator account, rather than a user's app: a lure.
strings.evidence[1].title: The Backup Log
strings.evidence[1].desc: Shows Karim Dawoud's phone connected to the garage's cell tower at the time of the crime: the line deleted from the main log.
strings.evidence[2].title: Line Deletion Record
strings.evidence[2].desc: A manual deletion at 23:20 under lead developer privileges, held only by Karim.
strings.evidence[3].title: Data Sale Contract
strings.evidence[3].desc: A deal selling users' location data to an advertising company for millions, concealed from the company.
strings.evidence[4].title: Dismissal Memo
strings.evidence[4].desc: A draft decision to fire Karim and inform the authorities, ready to be issued the next morning.
strings.suspects[0].name: Wissam, the Lead Investor
strings.suspects[0].alibi: "I was at a board meeting by video call. It was fully recorded."
strings.suspects[0].statement: I invested millions in Layan's vision, and her death sends my investment's value crashing. We disagreed about valuation, not life itself. I have no technical privileges. I barely use the app.
strings.suspects[1].name: Karim Dawoud
strings.suspects[1].relation: Her partner since the company was founded
strings.suspects[1].alibi: "I was working at the office on a server update all night."
strings.suspects[1].statement: Layan was my sister in this dream. We built every line together. Being accused of killing her tears me apart. Yes, I have full system privileges because I built it. Any log problem was a technical error during the update. The data is always protected by backups… as you know.
strings.suspects[2].name: Adel, the Disgruntled Driver
strings.suspects[2].relation: His account was suspended by the victim
strings.suspects[2].alibi: "I was making deliveries on the other side of the city. My route is recorded."
strings.suspects[2].statement: They unfairly suspended my account over one complaint, and I wrote to Layan in anger. But I was working that night. The app itself records all my movements minute by minute. That app knows more about me than I know about myself.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Guard at the Neighboring Garage
strings.witnesses[0].statement: I saw a sports car enter the abandoned garage near midnight and speed out half an hour later. I couldn't see its plate, but it was an expensive car that didn't belong there.
strings.witnesses[1].name: Team Developer
strings.witnesses[1].statement: Only Karim has permission to delete lines from the main log. He repeatedly warned us not to touch it. The backup is automatic and nobody can stop it, not even him.
strings.witnesses[2].name: The Victim's Secretary
strings.witnesses[2].statement: She had been tense lately and closed her office door for calls. She told me something cryptic: "Tomorrow everything will change… I've discovered something terrible about my partner."
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Body discovery report
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body: A garage cleaner reported a body on the ground floor. The phone and wallet were present.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic medicine
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Autopsy report
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body: Death from a forceful blow from behind with a hard object, between 22:45 and 23:10.
strings.folders[2].name: Digital Evidence
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Fake Request Analysis
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body: The request was created through an internal administrator interface using a developer account, not a user app: a deliberate lure.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Server Log Report
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body: At 23:20, a line linking a device to the garage's cell tower was deleted. The backup restored it and identified the device.
strings.folders[3].name: Interviews
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Karim Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body: An "update error" does not explain the selective manual deletion of one line. He evaded questions about the data contract.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: Investor Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body: His recorded meeting covers the critical window.
strings.folders[3].docs[2].title: Driver Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[2].body: His nighttime route is recorded in the app on the opposite side of the city.
strings.folders[4].name: Confidential files
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: Data Sale Contract
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body: Karim's encrypted email reveals the sale of location data to a third party for millions, without the company or investor knowing.
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: Confrontation Record
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body: Confronted with the backup, contract, and dismissal memo, Karim was silent for a long time, then said: "She was going to destroy everything I'd built."
strings.reports[0].title: Digital Crime Report
strings.reports[0].author: Cybercrime unit
strings.reports[0].body: A fake request used as a lure plus selective log deletion points to someone with lead developer privileges. The backup broke the plan.
strings.reports[1].title: Motive Report
strings.reports[1].author: Assigned investigator
strings.reports[1].body: The dismissal memo and data-sale contract provide an existential motive: murder to prevent both exposure and dismissal.
strings.notes[0].text: The app knows everyone's location — the killer's weapon
strings.notes[1].text: Who can precisely delete one line? Whoever holds the keys.
